Benchmarks

MerkleForge uses Criterion benchmarks in the unpublished merkle-bench crate to compare hash adapters, tree variants, proof generation, proof verification, and other Rust Merkle libraries. Criterion reports mean, median, and standard deviation to filter out noise.

Lower latency is better; higher throughput is better. For the latest CI numbers with links to every Criterion report, see the live benchmark explorer.

The tables below are copied from BENCHMARKS.md (run date 2026-08-17). That run predates the Unreleased sparse-tree and Patricia-trie performance fixes, which cut 4,000 sequential sparse inserts from about 223 s to 0.2 s and 4,000 Patricia inserts from about 5.9 s to 0.02 s. Sparse and Patricia numbers here are therefore pessimistic. Cells marked not captured were not completed in that run.

MerkleForge vs rs-merkle vs merkle_light

cargo bench --bench comparison

MetricMerkleForgers-merklemerkle_light
10K leaf construction22.77 ms3.69 ms2.29 ms
Proof size (10K tree)469 bytes448 bytes512 bytes
Proof verification1.84 µs6.39 µs1.78 µs
  • Construction uses deterministic 32-byte leaves for all libraries.
  • rs-merkle receives pre-hashed SHA-256 leaves, matching its public API.
  • Proof size is the serialized proof byte count reported by each library.

Reproduce

git clone https://github.com/1888-Labs/MerkleForge.git
cd MerkleForge
 
# Everything (long: the Patricia insert group alone can take many minutes)
cargo bench --workspace
xdg-open target/criterion/report/index.html   # `open` on macOS
 
# Focused groups
cargo bench --bench hash_throughput
cargo bench --bench binary_tree
cargo bench --bench sparse_tree
cargo bench --bench patricia_trie
cargo bench --bench comparison
cargo bench --bench bench_energy
 
# Print comparative proof sizes
MERKLEFORGE_PRINT_COMPARISON_SIZES=1 cargo bench --bench comparison -- --list

Record the machine, kernel, CPU governor, Rust version, and command next to any numbers you publish. Results are hardware-specific: compare trends across machines, not absolute values.

Reading the tables

  • Latency: time for one operation.
  • Throughput: bytes or elements processed per second.
  • Proof generation: time to produce the witness sent to a verifier.
  • Proof verification: time for a stateless client to check the witness against a trusted root.
  • Proof size: bytes sent over the network or stored as evidence.
